# `silk/raw_buffer`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Low-level typed views over owned allocations for implementing collections and storage actors.

## When to use
Prefer `silk.vector.Vector`, `silk.bytes.Bytes`, or `silk.box.Box` in application code. Use
these operations only when building a container that explicitly tracks capacity and which
slots are initialized.

## Details
[`copy`](#declaration-) supports overlapping ranges and behaves as though the moved elements passed through
temporary storage. [`fill`](#declaration-) writes raw bytes and therefore operates only on `RawBuffer<u8>`.

## Gotchas
[`from`](#declaration-), [`read`](#declaration-), [`copy`](#declaration-), [`view`](#declaration-), and [`viewMut`](#declaration-) are `unsafe`: the caller must prove
that an allocation fits the recorded element count, every selected range is in bounds, and
every read or view covers initialized elements. [`slot`](#declaration-) and [`fill`](#declaration-) check the recorded count
and trap outside it. Releasing a raw buffer releases its allocation but does not discover and
drop values still stored in it; a container must clear initialized `Slot` values before release.

## Examples
### Initialize and read a raw byte buffer
```silk
import silk.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

import silk.effect { Effect }

import silk.layout { Layout }

import silk.raw_buffer { RawBuffer }

import silk.u8

effect fn build() -> i32
! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let acquiring = Allocator.allocate(Layout.of<[u8; 3]>())
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let allocation = run acquiring
  unsafe {
    let mut buffer = RawBuffer.from<u8>(move allocation, 3)
    let filled = RawBuffer.fill(&mut buffer, 0, 3, u8.toU8(14))
    let values = RawBuffer.view<u8>(&buffer, 0, 3)
    return u8.toI32(values[0] + values[1] + values[2])
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn recover(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(build(), recover)
}
```

Import as `RawBuffer` with `import silk.raw_buffer { RawBuffer }`.

## `RawBuffer`

```silk
pub struct RawBuffer
```

The owner of the raw storage operations.

### Details

This struct carries no data and is never constructed by the library. Every operation is an
inherent member declared in `impl RawBuffer`, so `import silk.raw_buffer { RawBuffer }` is the
one import that reaches `RawBuffer.from(...)` and the rest. It is unrelated to the builtin
`RawBuffer<T>` type.

### Associated function `from`

```silk
pub unsafe fn from<T>(allocation: Intrinsic.Allocation, count: usize) -> Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>
```

Adopts an allocation as typed raw storage with the specified element capacity.

#### Gotchas

The caller must prove that the allocation has the size and alignment for `count` values of `T`.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `slot`

```silk
pub fn slot<'storage, T>(buffer: &'storage mut Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>, index: usize) -> Intrinsic.Slot<'storage, T>
```

Selects one raw storage slot after checking the buffer's recorded element count.

#### Gotchas

An `index` outside [`count`](#declaration-) traps. The slot operations that read or drop require the caller to
track whether the slot is initialized. The result retains exclusive access to the buffer until
the slot is consumed. Lifetimes inside `T` remain separate from this storage access.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `count`

```silk
pub fn count<T>(buffer: &Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>) -> usize
```

Returns the element capacity recorded by a raw buffer.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub unsafe fn read<T: Copy>(buffer: &Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>, index: usize) -> T
```

Copies one initialized element without changing its slot state.

#### Gotchas

The caller must prove that `index` is less than [`count`](#declaration-) and that the selected slot contains
an initialized `T`. A copied reference retains its original referent lifetime after the buffer
is released.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `copy`

```silk
pub unsafe fn copy<T>(destination: &mut Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>, destinationOffset: usize, source: &[T], length: usize) -> ()
```

Moves a caller-proven initialized range into selected storage in one bulk transfer.

#### Details

Source and destination may overlap; the result is as if the elements travelled through an
intermediate buffer.

#### Gotchas

The caller must prove that both selected ranges are in bounds. The source range must be
initialized.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `fill`

```silk
pub fn fill(buffer: &mut Intrinsic.RawBuffer<u8>, offset: usize, length: usize, value: u8) -> ()
```

Initializes a selected byte range with one repeated byte value.

#### Gotchas

A range beyond [`count`](#declaration-) traps.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `view`

```silk
pub unsafe fn view<T>(buffer: &Intrinsic.RawBuffer<T>, offset: usize, length: usize) -> &[T]
```

Borrows a shared view of an initialized element range.

#### Gotchas

The caller must prove that the selected range is in bounds and that each selected slot is
initialized.

<a id="declaration-"></a>
